topicData.topic: The AI spending-to-revenue gap is being ignored by everyone building these systems. $725B spent in 2026, $75B earned. Companies are pricing laptops higher because chip demand from data centres is insane, but nobody's asking who actually pays back this bet.
topicData.angle: Your MacBook got 18% more expensive this month because someone bet $725 billion that AI would print money. It hasn't. And nobody's talking about what happens when that bet breaks.

postText:
MacBook Air just went up 18%. No new product. No big announcement. Just a price hike, mid-year, because components cost too much.

The components cost too much because every data centre on earth is chasing the same chips.

The chips are being hoarded because someone made a $725 billion bet that AI would print money by now.

It hasn't. The whole industry earned $75 billion this year against that spend. That's not a gap. That's a prayer.

And somehow the cost of that prayer is landing on my laptop.

I didn't expect to feel this one personally. But there it is. Apple raises prices, Xbox raises prices, and the official reason is "component costs." Which is true. But the reason components cost that much is a story nobody's telling out loud.

Ray Dalio is calling it a bubble. So is Michael Burry. The dot-com crash had $500B in unused fibre underground. This is running at 10 times that scale.

I genuinely don't know when or how this corrects. But I'd like to know who's holding the bill when it does.
